pass.text: With zero same-clip controls, stock TRIBE v2's language readout was stronger when the same healthy listeners heard a public story intact than when they heard its sentences shuffled (Narratives notthefall, 22 listeners, 9.1 minutes = 365 TRs per version; the order of their two runs is not public).

Each version also had its own TRIBE forecast, so a pass does not separate a change in the listeners' brains from a change in TRIBE's forecast, and the run order is not public, so it cannot be separated from an order or repeat-listening effect. Intact vs the coarser scramble (descriptive): HL 0.0215 [95% CI -0.0068, 0.0538], p = 0.0735, 21 listeners, 9.1 minutes = 365 TRs per version; did not reach p < 0.05.

vo.text: Labs study people who can't respond after brain injury by playing them stories in the scanner.
But every new story needs its own 12-15 healthy volunteers scanned first, in that language.
For a new story, StillHere gives labs a first reading with zero volunteer scans, measured against each listener's own brain.
It has been tested only in healthy volunteers.
A researcher types the study they want.
Muse Spark 1.3 turns it into a plan from a tested menu.
Ask about one patient's scan, and it declines, with the reason.
On 62 unseen requests, it wrongly accepted 2.3 percent; Spark Open, 7.6 and 6.8.
StillHere cuts the story at sentence boundaries.
Voice Transcribe hears 98 percent of the words, reordered.
Our first word scramble failed this check.
Spark Open adds a second opinion on the conditions. It is advisory, and never blocks a build.
